item.title: poster · described

turns.text: Make one image, aspect 9:16, from this exact description: Vertical vintage screen-printed travel poster, straight-on, filling the frame within a narrow charcoal surround. An aged ivory paper border has stained corners, tiny dark pinholes, scuffs, and uneven edges. The upper four-fifths shows a canyon from a high overlook, looking slightly downward. Layered flat-topped mesas recede toward a high horizon; a broad distant butte sits above center. Huge stepped cliffs fill both foreground sides, enclosing a deep, zigzagging central gorge. A thin pale sage river winds upward from the lower left-center into shadow. Jagged rock faces have angular cracks, narrow vertical orange edges, and scattered cream patches across dusty salmon ledges. Flat inks: peach pink, pale yellow-green, muted sage, gray lavender, burnt orange, and near-black navy. Pale sky with broad salmon clouds and thin horizontal streaks. Upper-left illumination leaves deep navy shadows on right-facing cliffs; no gradients. Rough ink registration, grainy paper, simplified hard-edged shapes. A salmon bottom panel carries centered dark navy uppercase lettering: small spaced “A FREE GOVERNMENT SERVICE” above large wide “GRAND CANYON”; below, “NATIONAL” at left and “PARK” at right. Bottom-left reads “U.S. DEPARTMENT” then “OF THE INTERIOR”; bottom-right reads “NATIONAL PARK” then “SERVICE”. Between them sits a navy circular seal containing a bison silhouette, pale mountain lines, and a dotted inner rim. Lettering is bold, geometric, slightly irregular.

must_haves: A poster image matching the prompt.
